name: Independence Palace
summary: The modernist presidential palace of South Vietnam. On 30 April 1975 a tank crashed through its gates, and the war ended.

eras.title: Norodom Palace
eras.text: The French built a grand palace here for the Governor of Cochinchina, completed in the 1870s and named after King Norodom of Cambodia. This photograph shows it in 1896.

image.file: 1896 - Cochinchine - Saïgon - Palais du Gouvernement Général.jpg

eras.label: 1920s
eras.title: Seat of the governors
eras.text: Under French rule the palace hosted governors and official visitors, like Governor-General Alexandre Varenne in the 1920s.

image.file: Toàn quyền Alexandre Varenne tại Saigon - Dinh Norodom.jpg
image.alt: Governor-General Varenne at the Norodom Palace

eras.title: A modern palace
eras.text: After the old palace was badly damaged in a bombing attack on President Ngô Đình Diệm in 1962, it was pulled down. A new palace designed by architect Ngô Viết Thụ opened in 1966.

eras.label: 30 April 1975
eras.title: The gates fall
eras.text: Just before noon on 30 April 1975, tanks of the North Vietnamese army broke through the gates. The last president of South Vietnam surrendered, and the war ended.

eras.label: Today
eras.title: A museum of an era
eras.text: The palace is kept almost exactly as it was in 1975: meeting rooms, banquet halls, a rooftop helipad and a basement war room full of maps and radios.

story.title: A palace of light and shade
story.narration: Ngô Viết Thụ, the architect, was the first Vietnamese to win the Grand Prix de Rome, a top French architecture prize. For the new palace, he combined modernist lines with Vietnamese ideas. A screen of concrete 'bamboo' shades the front, letting in air and light while keeping out the sun. Fans of feng shui say the building's outline forms Chinese characters for good fortune and prosperity. Built in the middle of a war, it was meant to show a confident, modern Vietnam.

story.title: 30 April 1975
story.narration: On the morning of 30 April 1975, North Vietnamese tanks raced into Saigon. Tank 843 hit the side gate of the palace and stuck; tank 390 smashed straight through the main gate. Soldiers ran up the steps and raised a flag on the roof. Inside, President Dương Văn Minh, who had been in office for just two days, and his cabinet were waiting. That afternoon he announced the surrender on the radio. Both tanks are now kept as national treasures, and replicas stand in the palace grounds.

story.title: Rooms of power

image.alt: The war room in the basement

story.narration: Visitors can walk through the palace almost as its staff left it. Upstairs are the cabinet room, reception halls decorated with lacquer paintings, the president's living quarters and a cinema. On the roof is a helipad with a helicopter. In the basement, behind thick concrete, are the telecommunications centre and war room, with old radios, telephones and wall maps of the battlefields. Walking through them, the last years of South Vietnam feel very close.

story.title: A walk through the palace

video.alt: Video tour of the rooms of the Independence Palace in Ho Chi Minh City

story.narration: A tour of the palace, filmed in 2016. The building was designed by Ngô Viết Thụ, the first Vietnamese architect to win the Prix de Rome, and opened in 1966 as the home and office of the president of South Vietnam. After 30 April 1975 it was left much as it was, so the reception halls, private apartments and the war room in the basement still look as they did then. Signs in Vietnamese, English and French guide visitors from room to room.

guide.price: Small entry ticket; audio guides available.

hours.notes: Approximate. Last entry earlier; may close at lunchtime.

do: Dress modestly; this is a national monument.
Combine with Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office nearby.
Go in the morning before the heat.
dont: Sit on the furniture or cross the ropes.
Use a drone over the city centre.

tips.title: Saigon food
tips.text: Cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork), bánh mì and bún thịt nướng; coffee on a tiny plastic stool.

tips.title: Getting there
tips.text: In District 1. Bến Thành metro station is a 10-minute walk.

tips.title: Nearby
tips.text: Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Central Post Office, Bến Thành market and the War Remnants Museum.
